title: Every new io2 volume is Block Express (cap 256,000 IOPS, was 64,000) — iopsPerGB io2 StorageClasses may provision more

detection.reason: StorageClass parameters are not collected yet (Storage tab slice); the hint names the EBS CSI StorageClasses

quote: The `blockExpress` StorageClass parameter is deprecated, effective immediately
remediation: From v1.47 every new io2 volume is Block Express and the io2 IOPS cap is 256,000 (64,000 before, unless the StorageClass set blockExpress): an io2 StorageClass that sizes IOPS by iopsPerGB, or asks for more than 64,000, now provisions more IOPS — and costs more. Set an explicit iops on those StorageClasses to bound cost. The blockExpress parameter itself is ignored (a deprecation log line) — remove it. Volumes above 64,000 IOPS may not reach full performance on non-Nitro instances.
verifyCommand: kubectl get storageclass -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.provisioner == "ebs.csi.aws.com") | "\(.metadata.name): \(.parameters // {} | to_entries | map("\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(" "))"'  # type=io2 with iopsPerGB or iops above 64000 now provisions more; blockExpress=… is ignored from v1.47
coversNotes: URGENT (1.47.0): Starting in v1.47.0, newly created io2 volumes will always use a cap of 256,000 IOPS,
